page: Microsoft Azure D32ds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with an x86_64 architecture. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and is equipped with a 260 MB L3 cache. The server is provisioned with 128.0 GB of system memory, translating to 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Additionally, it includes 1890 GB of local storage and supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark evaluations show strong performance in specific workloads. The server achieves top-tier results in LLM inference text generation for small models, reaching 355.44 tokens per second. It also registers strong performance in static web serving throughput at 56.21 GB per second, and in CPU physics testing. However, memory subsystem performance presents a notable tradeoff, with the PassMark memory score falling into the bottom 25% of tested systems, despite a read-only cached small block memory bandwidth of 2484.25 GB per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D32ds_v6 offers a balanced resource density for general-purpose workloads requiring dedicated compute resources and substantial local storage. The inclusion of a 1890 GB local disk reduces the need for external storage attachments for temporary data. This hardware profile is appropriate for database operations, static web serving, software compilation, and moderate language model inference tasks.
